facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The excavations in Sinauli were conducted by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) from 2005-2006 and in mid-2018.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India carried out excavations at Sinauli in the Baghpat district during 2005–2006 and mid-2018.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: According to the ¹⁴C radiocarbon dating and recovered material culture, the site date back to 4000 yr BP (∼2000 BCE) and is thought to belong to Ochre-Coloured Pottery (OCP)/Copper Hoard culture.
facts.text: Radiocarbon dating places the Sinauli burials and organic cultural material at approximately 2000 to 1800 BCE, around 4,000 years before present.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The excavation team reportedly found two cart-like vehicles and eight well-preserved corpses in coffins that appeared to have been mounted on a pedestal.
facts.text: Archaeologists excavated eight burial pits at the site containing wooden coffins mounted on legs with lids featuring anthropomorphic figures.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: In his opinion, several indications suggest that the Sanauli “chariots” are actually carts yoked to bulls, as in the copper sculpture of a bull-cart from the Late Harappan site of Daimabad in Maharashtra.
facts.text: While ASI excavation director Sanjay Manjul identified the vehicles as horse-drawn war chariots, Indologist Asko Parpola argued that their solid wheels indicate ox-drawn carts.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Several scholars have noted that solid wheels belong to carts, not chariots.
facts.text: Historians dispute whether the vehicles meet the technological criteria of chariots, because classical war chariots require light spoked wheels rather than solid wooden discs.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: According to Asko Parpola, these finds were ox-pulled carts, indicating that these burials are related to an early Aryan migration of Proto-Indo-Iranian speaking people into the Indian subcontinent.
facts.text: Researchers disagree on whether Sinauli represents a local development of the Copper Hoard culture or an early wave of Indo-Iranian pastoralists migrating into northern India.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Give us just five villages, Duryodhana, and we will be content.
facts.text: In the Mahabharata's Udyoga Parva, peace emissaries propose that granting five specific villages to the Pandavas would resolve the territorial conflict without war.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Baghpat was originally known as Vyaghraprastha ('tiger city') and is traditionally regarded as one of the five villages demanded by the Pandavas.
facts.text: Local traditions in western Uttar Pradesh associate the modern town of Baghpat with Vyaghraprastha, one of the five villages requested by the Pandavas in the epic tradition.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Local legends tell that Sinauli is one of the five villages that god Krishna unsuccessfully negotiated with the Kaurava princes to avoid the War at Kurukshetra.
facts.text: Popular narratives and local folklore identify the Sinauli warriors and wheeled vehicles directly as physical remains of the Mahabharata conflict.
